rows.statement: Today we have an update regarding which spells we are going to be flagging as non-secret for Midnight launch. These changes are planned to go out in a data hotfix in the next couple days, but we wanted to give you all a heads up beforehand so you can plan any necessary changes to your addons.
rows.proof_level: metadata
rows.next_proof: Editorial/source/build context or external resource link; no runtime credit.

rows.statement: Over the course of Beta, as well as recent weeks on live, one of the biggest recurring points of feedback has been from healers who wish that our default UI provided more robust options for filtering or emphasizing specific buffs on raid frames. In the past month we have added a few layers of extra logic to buff sorting and visibility, and while we've heard positive feedback from many healers about these improvements, we realize that our solutions are leaving others still wanting more customization.
rows.proof_level: metadata
rows.next_proof: Editorial/source/build context or external resource link; no runtime credit.

rows.statement: While we had originally hoped to be able to deliver a streamlined default experience, it has become clear that there are common use-cases that a single set of logic cannot cover. Some players may want to make simple tweaks like highlighting the target of their Preservation Evoker's Echo, or their Holy Paladin's active Beacon, while others would consider that to be distracting clutter. We are now beginning work on a system to allow players to hide or emphasize buffs from their spellcasts on a per-spell basis, via the Spellbook. We expect that solution to be ready for players in a later Midnight patch.
rows.proof_level: metadata
rows.next_proof: Editorial/source/build context or external resource link; no runtime credit.

rows.statement: In the meantime, we have also seen a few addons popping up that use non-secret information to make very reliable guesses about players' spellcasts in order to drive this sort of filtering logic. Breaking the API calls driving this functionality would cause significant collateral damage to common addons, and we are not planning to do go down that path. Ultimately, this design space is mostly about customizing the display of information, rather than objectively advantageous computational solutions, so we want to treat it the same way we approached resources like Holy Power or Maelstrom.
rows.proof_level: metadata
rows.next_proof: Editorial/source/build context or external resource link; no runtime credit.

rows.statement: Thus, rather than requiring addon developers to jump through hoops to support an implementation that will have some frustrating inaccuracies, we are planning to flag a number of short-cooldown rotational healer spells, and very long duration buffs, to exclude them from our Secret Value system. We will likely re-protect these spells once our own filtering solution, with its own addon hooks for display customization, is in place.
rows.proof_level: source/test-body inspection only; no new runtime acceptance

rows.statement: Hello again from Blizzard! Mythic raids and M+ open this week and we will be hotfixing in some last-minute changes to fix exploits before resets.
rows.proof_level: metadata
rows.next_proof: Editorial/source/build context or external resource link; no runtime credit.

rows.statement: We recognize that some of these changes are going to be disruptive and require last-second changes to your addons, and we sincerely apologize for them coming in so late. Part of these changes involve removing the secure delegate portion of ActionButton_ApplyCooldown. We have added new APIs that should replace the functionality it provided, but we will be watching closely for reports of functionality that still needs replacing.
